recommendation: Existing-reservation-only d_cfv_slot hints are a bounded design, but actual graph inheritance and scoped pre-free normalization remain unresolved. Do not activate E033 or prepare a primary cohort from capacity alone. A separately authorized execution/attribute proof and reviewed cleanup design must precede any production candidate.

observed_capacity.scope: One successful getter-only process,17 CUresult0 calls including cleanup. Current limit is that process context, not a promise about a solver/server context. Positive capacity is not a cache miss or speed measurement.

single_prospective_policy.allocation: GpuSolver::d_cfv_slot, complete existing immutable u32 allocation
single_prospective_policy.base_ptr: actual owned allocation base, not an inferred pointer
single_prospective_policy.num_bytes: checked d_cfv_slot.len()*4; no prefix truncation or alternate window
single_prospective_policy.eligibility: Nonempty complete allocation; query actual solver-context current limit and device max window; enable only when complete byte length <= both, with supported successful APIs. Otherwise exact unhinted path. Never hardcode the observed18MiB or enlarge reservation. Unsupported/error must be distinguishable from zero.
single_prospective_policy.allocation_and_kernel_math_changes: No new data payload or arithmetic is implied by the hint itself. The needed cleanup path may add a read-only kernel and synchronization; that is additional scope, not part of an already implemented one-line change.
single_prospective_policy.not_a_capacity_guarantee: A per-allocation fit does not reserve exclusive L2 space. Overlapping solver windows/other kernels can compete even without limit setters.

capture_gate.intended_setup: Set the private solver stream window after all immutable metadata is allocated and before any eager use or capture, including nonzero warm/resumed constructors. Query it back.
capture_gate.required_evidence: Inspect captured kernel-node access-policy attributes for both player training graphs and raked/unraked evaluation graphs; verify exact base/bytes/hitRatio/properties before treating capture inheritance as established. A stream GetAttribute result or successful replay alone is insufficient.
capture_gate.immediate_instantiation: cudarc safe/graph.rs54-68 ends capture and immediately instantiates. The retained graph getter can inspect captured attributes, but a later graph-node setter cannot be assumed to modify the executable. If inheritance fails, stop this variant rather than silently adding a different capture pipeline.
capture_gate.paths: First eager iteration, profiled eager iteration, first eager evaluation, subsequent captured evaluation, warm first capture, lock-triggered graph replacement and standalone continuation must retain the intended scope. The hint should not be rebound to swapped mutable workspace buffers.

cleanup_gate.official_contract: The NVIDIA guide distinguishes disabling a window from clearing old persisting lines, describes NORMAL accesses as a scoped normalization mechanism, and discourages waiting for automatic reset. The memory-free contract documents allocation lifetime/synchronization but supplies no persistence-priority normalization guarantee.
cleanup_gate.current_drop: GpuSolver has no custom Drop. Its d_cfv_slot field precedes graph fields; implicit field teardown is not an explicit cache cleanup contract. CudaSlice Drop uses same-stream free_async when supported, otherwise stream synchronize then free. CudaGraph Drop destroys executable and graph. Neither wrapper normalizes persisting priorities.
cleanup_gate.minimum_required_order: While the owned allocation is still live: stop further solver submissions; drain existing stream work; retire graph handles that reference the window; normalize the owned window with NORMAL accesses; synchronize that normalization; disable the stream window and verify the final attribute; only then free the allocation. No graph may subsequently launch with the old window pointer.
cleanup_gate.normalization_not_proven: Setting NORMAL in a stream attribute only controls future work; this report does not claim that the setter alone touches old cache lines. A complete read-only access pass over the owned allocation under NORMAL is a plausible scoped mechanism requiring explicit implementation/source review and execution/error checks. No such pass is implemented or run here; no API getter proves physical line residency/priorities.
forbidden_shortcuts: Assume cuMemFree/free_async or stream destruction normalizes priorities
Use a global persisting-L2 reset per solver
Save/set/restore the shared context limit per solver
Report only a best-effort destructor without surfacing cleanup failure in qualification
cleanup_gate.engineering_boundary: This needs a real ownership/teardown path, potentially a small cleanup kernel and explicit fallible close plus destructor fallback, not just an attribute setter. Rust field reordering alone is insufficient. If reliable pre-free normalization/error handling requires broader ownership redesign, defer this optimization; no broad redesign is authorized.

lifecycle_constraints: The metadata allocation stays fixed across the seven-buffer continuation/paging swaps. Distinct solver/board instances own distinct allocations and need separate attribute lifetimes.
Lock updates drain work and replace captured graphs, but do not replace d_cfv_slot. New captures still require correct inherited attributes; never retain references beyond solver destruction.

Constructor failure after enabling a window, capture failure, interrupted work, cleanup error and repeated solver creation/drop need explicit handling. A device error can prevent cleanup; qualification must preserve/report it rather than assert normalization.

Shared-context peers must not have their limits or whole-cache priority reset. Scoped reads of the uniquely owned allocation are the candidate isolation mechanism; concurrent L2 contention remains possible.

The frozen primary cycle excludes final destruction. Any new cleanup work must be measured and disclosed in an additional whole-process/lifetime observation before acceptance; do not silently claim a full-lifetime saving or move existing solve work beyond the score boundary.
smallest_next_evidence_if_authorized: First a bounded capture-attribute/lifetime feasibility check, using existing diagnostic patterns rather than a new framework. Setting policy before capture then inspecting original captured nodes can be checked without replay and therefore without creating persisting cache data. Any later replay must include the scoped cleanup path, raw immutable-buffer/state equality, full error/cleanup evidence and repeated construct/drop coverage. No performance conclusion follows. Root must authorize actual execution separately.
exactness_and_performance_limits: The proposed policy does not change source floating arithmetic, but source reasoning and capacity do not substitute for executed exact state comparisons. An eventual E033 would still require independent native equivalence before fixed primary gates, then broader/full-state/F32/continuation and fresh cumulative controls only if qualifying. No >=2% benefit, cache miss rate, hit rate or native timing share is established.
